column1: # PostgreSQL-style SQL prototype: the accept and reject corpus (grammar issue #3, harness issue #2).
# Columns, separated by one TAB: id, scope, statement, expected.
# id: unique, lower case, words joined by hyphens. Add a case at the end of its group; never renumber or reuse an id.

# scope: in = the statement lies inside the subset of the grammar, out = it lies outside. With the outcome read from the server the engine must parse an in statement that the server parsed, refuse an out statement that the server parsed with SQLSTATE 0A000, and refuse a statement that the server rejected as syntax-error 42601 with 42601, whatever its scope.
# statement: one statement, with backslash, tab, line feed and carriage return written as \\, \t, \n and \r.

# expected: written by the generator from the real server, never by hand. ok = the server parsed the statement. syntax-error 42601 = the server rejected it as a syntax error. error SQLSTATE = the server parsed it and a later stage refused it (an unknown table, an undetermined parameter type), which counts as parsed. Empty = the generator has not run on the case yet: add a case with an empty expected, then run the generator.

# generator: the integration test PgParityIT of the e2e module with -Dpgparity.regenerate=true, or the workflow PostgreSQL prototype - answer parity started by hand with regenerate on. The server only parses a statement here (the parse step of the protocol), it never runs one.
# readers: the harness (answer parity of issue #2) and the parser tests (issue #3), through com.arcadedb.query.postgresql.corpus.Corpus.
# server: PostgreSQL 18.7 (Debian 18.7-1.pgdg13+5) on x86_64-pc-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit
